Overview & City Profile

Calvià (Calvià (Illes Balears)) is a municipality in Illes Balears, Balearic Islands (coordinates 39.5633°N, 2.503°E; population 51,114). Visitors use Calvià as a base to explore Balearic Islands's historic town centers, regional markets, and culinary specialties such as Ensaïmada de Mallorca, Sobrasada & Tumbet, Caldereta de langosta (Menorca).

Within Balearic Islands Region (Illes Balears region), Calvià (Calvià (Illes Balears)) serves as a municipio (municipality) in balearic islands region. Travelers exploring Balearic Islands often combine a stop in Calvià with regional highlights such as Palma Cathedral (La Seu) & Serra de Tramuntana, Sóller, Valldemossa & Deià, Menorca Ciutadella & virgin calas, Ibiza Dalt Vila (UNESCO) & Formentera.

Getting to Calvià & Getting Around

Via the regional hub (Palma de Mallorca Central Station (Renfe AVE, Iryo & Ouigo High-Speed Rail)): Palma de Mallorca (PMI), Ibiza (IBZ) and Menorca (MAH) airports; Baleària & Trasmed ferries from Barcelona, Valencia and Dénia.

  • Local rail & IC cards: Once in Balearic Islands Region, JR regional lines and local private railways connect Palma de Mallorca with Calvià. Nationwide IC cards (Transit Card, Pasmo, Icoca) work on major urban and JR commuter gates; for rural branch lines or local buses, keep €1,000 bills and €100 coins handy for the onboard fare box.
  • Luggage & station lockers: Main stations in Balearic Islands have coin lockers for day-trippers. If you are stopping in Calvià en route between larger bases, check your suitcase dimensions in our Luggage & Locker Checker or forward big bags ahead with Takkyubin.
  • Driving & car rental: While city centers around Calvià are accessible by train and taxi, renting a car from a major Renfe AVE, Iryo & Ouigo High-Speed Rail station or airport in Balearic Islands can be rewarding for reaching mountain gorges, coastal viewpoints, and countryside onsen. Read our Renting a Car in Spain Guide.

Best Time to Visit & Seasonal Highlights

Best time to visit Balearic Islands: Apr–Jun, Sep–Oct.

Regional highlights across Balearic Islands Region that pair well with a visit to Calvià include: Palma Cathedral (La Seu) & Serra de Tramuntana, Sóller, Valldemossa & Deià, Menorca Ciutadella & virgin calas, Ibiza Dalt Vila (UNESCO) & Formentera.

Practical Travel Tips for Calvià

  • Tourist information center (観光案内所): Look for the Kankō Annaijo counter inside or right outside the main train station in Calvià (or at Palma de Mallorca Central Station (Renfe AVE, Iryo & Ouigo High-Speed Rail)) for free walking maps, bus timetables, and festival calendars.
  • Cash & ATMs: While hotels, chain stores, and convenience stores in Calvià accept international cards and IC payment, smaller family-run restaurants, shrines, and rural buses often prefer cash. 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) and Spain Post ATMs accept foreign debit cards reliably.
  • Dining hours: Outside major metropolitan hubs, lunch typically runs 11:30 AM–2:00 PM and dinner spots open around 5:30 PM, with earlier last orders (around 8:00–9:00 PM) in smaller cities.

Frequently asked questions

Where is Calvià (Calvià (Illes Balears)) located in Spain?

Calvià (Calvià (Illes Balears)) is a municipio (municipality) located in Balearic Islands Region in the Illes Balears region of Spain (coordinates: 39.5633°N, 2.503°E). It has a population of approximately 51,114 across an area of Regional km².

How do I get to Calvià by train?

Most visitors reach Calvià via the main prefectural gateway of Palma de Mallorca Central Station (Renfe AVE, Iryo & Ouigo High-Speed Rail). Palma de Mallorca (PMI), Ibiza (IBZ) and Menorca (MAH) airports; Baleària & Trasmed ferries from Barcelona, Valencia and Dénia. From the regional hub, connect by JR local/rapid lines, private commuter railways, or local bus to Calvià. You can estimate long-distance rail costs using our Renfe AVE, Iryo & Ouigo High-Speed Rail Fare Calculator.

What local food is Calvià and Balearic Islands known for?

In Calvià and across Balearic Islands Region, top local dishes include Ensaïmada de Mallorca, Sobrasada & Tumbet, Caldereta de langosta (Menorca), as well as Bullit de peix (Ibiza) and Sóller oranges & Binissalem wines. Look for local ekiben (station bento boxes), morning markets, and family-run shokudo near the main station.

When is the best time of year to visit Calvià?

Best time to visit Balearic Islands: Apr–Jun, Sep–Oct. Check our Spain Seasonal Calendar to compare month-by-month weather and crowd levels.
